newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: WARNING OF CUT BACKS TO FAMILY COURT BUDGET
The Federal Opposition says cutbacks to the family court budget are being felt hardest in regional areas.
Spokesman for Justice and Attorney General, Senator Nick Bolkus, says backlogs are building in north Queensland where the cuts have meant a loss of four weeks court time.
Senator Bolkus says the lack of access is compounded by the long distances to courts and the additional expense of legal representation in the regions.
He says there are stories of some people not being able to take their partners to court, and people with intellectual disabilities having to represent themselves.
PORT ARTHUR VICTIMS TO KNOW SOON ON COMPENSATION
Victims of the Port Arthur shootings should know early next month how much compensation they'll receive from the national appeal. More than A$3.5 million has been donated to the appeal.
About A$340,000 has already been distributed.
The Victims Appeal Committee is now in the final stages of deciding who should get what. The money is expected to be distributed around January the tenth.
OPPOSITION LEADER SAYS PM HAS A LOT OF EXPLAINING
Federal Opposition Leader Kim Beazley says the Prime Minister has a lot of explaining to do when he makes his end of year report to the nation.
The Prime Minister will address Parliament this afternoon.
Mr Beazley says Mr Howard should confirm comments by Federal Treasurer Peter Costello in Sydney last night that unemployment is not improving as fast as the Government had hoped.
Mr Beazley says the Prime Minister won't be able to report many kept election promises.
INDEPENDENT MP SAYS ELECTION WAS ON THE CARDS OVER TELSTRA
Independent Senator Brian Harradine says the Federal Government would have called an election next April if he hadn't agreed to vote for the part sale of Telstra.
Senator Harradine agreed to vote with the government in exchange for an assistance package for Tasmania.
He told the ABC's Graeme Denmead that by voting for the sale of one-third of Telstra, he stopped the government going for a full sale after an early election.
HEALTH MINISTERS SAYS NO AGREEMENT ON HEALTH REFORMS
Federal Health Minister, Michael Wooldridge, says he hasn't yet reached agreement with the Australian Democrats about the proposed limit on medicare provider numbers for new GPs.
He's expected to announce a compromise today to meet Democrat concerns over the impact of the cuts on mecical students, to ensure the changes pass the Senate.
Junior Doctors in New South Wales, the ACT and South Australia are on strike for a day in protest at the Government's move to restrict the number of new GPs.
Dr Wooldridge has told ABC radio, he is considering proposals to allow 300 more training places for GPs, especially in rural medicine.
NT POLICE LOOKING FOR SUSPECTS OVER SHOOTING
Northern Territory Police say they're looking for two men believed responsible for the shooting of four people at Numbulwar in Eastern Arnhem Land overnight.
Two of the injured were flown to Nhulunbuy Hospital, while a woman and a young boy were treated at the Numbulwar Clinic.
Acting Superintendent Max Pope, says Detectives from Darwin have flown to Numbulwar and road blocks have been set up as it's believed the two offenders have left the Numbulwar community.
PAKISTAN CRICKET TEAM ARRIVES IN AUSTRALIA
The Pakistan cricket team arrived in Adelaide this morning to prepare for their one-day international series against Australia and the West Indies.
The series will bring together two of the world's best leg-spin bowlers -- Australia's Shane Warne and Pakistan's Mushtaq Ahmed.
Pakistan captain Wasim Akram says Mushtaq has genuine claims to be number one.
CROCODILE DUNDEE AND PIG BABE TOP ALL-TIME LIST
Two Australian-made films, Crocodile Dundee and Babe, have topped the survey for the all-time top five films in Australia, as of May this year.
The survey appears in a new publication from the Australian Film Commission, called "Get The Picture".
It shows Australia produced an average of 30 feature films a year during the eighties, and 25 a year during the first half of the nineties.
As of May 1996, the all-time top five films in Australia were Crocodile Dundee, Babe, Jurassic Park, E.T. and Forrest Gump.
